title: Daiso Recalls Children's Coin Purses and Jewelry Due to Risk of Lead Exposure
summary: The surface paint on the zippers of the coin purses and the clasps on the jewelry contain high levels of lead. Lead is toxic if ingested by young children and can cause adverse health effects. Units: About 190.

title: Tekkeon Inc. Recalls MyPower ALL Plus External Laptop Batteries Due to Fire Hazard
summary: The battery cell can short-circuit and overheat, posing a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 500.

title: Baja Motorsports Recalls Mini Bikes and Go-Carts Due to Fire and Burn Hazards
summary: The gas cap can leak or detach from the fuel tank on the recalled mini bikes and go-carts, posing a fire and burn hazard to consumers. In addition, the throttle can stick due to an improperly positioned fuel line and throttle cable, posing a sudden acceleration hazard to consumers. Units: About 308,

title: Child’s Death Prompts Recall to Repair Portable Playard Tent by Tots in Mind Due to Strangulation Hazard
summary: Clips that attach the tent to the top of the playard can break or be removed by a child. A child can lift the tent and become entrapped at the neck between the rigid playard frame and the metal base rod of the tent, posing a strangulation hazard. Units: About 20,000 (and 85 in Canada).

title: Muddy Outdoors Recalls Climbing Sticks Due to Fall Hazard
summary: Bolts that secure the cam locks to the frame of these climbing sticks that retains the rope around the tree can break, allowing the cam locks to detach from the frame. Units: Approximately 2,550.

title: Pottery Barn Kids Recalls to Repair Drop-Side Cribs Due to Entrapment, Suffocation and Fall Hazards
summary: The cribs' drop-sides can detach when hardware breaks, creating a space into which a young child can become entrapped, which can lead to suffocation. A child can also fall out of the crib. Drop side incidents also occur due to incorrect assembly and with age-related wear and tear. Units: About 82,00

title: Snow Blowers Recalled by The Toro Company Due to Fire Hazard
summary: Exposure to ethanol in gasoline can cause the carburetor needle to become corroded. A corroded needle can stick in the open position and allow fuel to leak from the carburetor, posing a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 35,700 in the United States and 2,300 in Canada.

title: Seattle Bike Supply Recalls Bicycles and Framesets Due to Fall Hazard
summary: The bicycle fork's legs can separate from the fork crown and cause the rider to lose control, posing a fall hazard and risk of injury. Units: About 330.

title: Tween Brands Recalls Children's Metal Jewelry Due to High Levels of Cadmium
summary: The children's metal jewelry contains high levels of cadmium. Cadmium is toxic if ingested by children and can cause adverse health effects. Units: About 137,000.

title: Wire Feed Welders Recalled by Star Asia USA Due to Burn Hazard
summary: The wire welder's torch does not have a cold contactor as erroneously stated on the packaging and instruction manual. Without this feature, the welder generates an electrical arc immediately upon contact with the welding material, posing a burn hazard to consumers. Units: About 9,000.

title: All Terrain Vehicles Recalled by American Suzuki Motor Corp. Due to Loss of Control Hazard
summary: The flame arrester screen can become detached from its mounting ring, preventing the throttle valve from returning to the idle position when the throttle lever is released and causing the rider to lose control of the ATV. This poses a serious hazard of injury or death. Units: About 1,355.

title: PDi Communications Recalls Televisions Installed in Healthcare Facilities Due to Fire Hazard
summary: A capacitor on the television's power supply board can fail, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 2,700.

title: Campus Cruisers Recalls Bicycles Due to Front Fork Failure
summary: The bicycle's front fork can crack or break, causing a sudden loss of steering control and posing a fall hazard to bicyclists. Units: About 100.

title: Marley Engineered Products Recalls Baseboard Heaters Sold at Grainger Due to Fire Hazard
summary: The baseboard heaters are labeled for 240 or 208 volt use. However, some of the heaters have an internal heater built for a maximum of 120 volts. If the heater is connected to a 240 or 208 volt electrical circuit as directed, the unit could catch fire. Units: About 30.

title: Recall to Repair: Whitco Company LP Stadium Light Poles Can Fall Over, Posing Risk of Serious Injury and Death
summary: Collapse Units: More than 2,500.

title: Husqvarna Professional Products Recalls Riding Lawn Tractors Due to Fire Hazard
summary: The fuel line on the rear-mounted fuel tank is too long and can come in contact with moving parts while the tractor is in use, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 1,700.

title: Baby Matters Recalls Nap Nanny® Recliners Due to Entrapment, Suffocation and Fall Hazards; One Infant Death Reported
summary: Infants can partially fall or hang over the side of the Nap Nanny® even while the harness is in use. title: Brine Recalls VIP Lacrosse Gloves Due to Violation of Lead Paint Standard
summary: Screen printing ink used on the silver triad logo on the back of the glove contains excessive levels of lead, violating the federal lead paint standard. Units: About 7,000 in the United States and 30 in Canada.

title: Near Strangulation Prompts Recall of Roman and Roller Shades by Smith+Noble
summary: Roman Shades: Strangulations can occur when a child places his/her neck between the exposed inner cord and the fabric on the backside of the shade or when a child pulls the cord out and wraps it around his/her neck. title: Atico International USA Recalls Bamboo Torches Due to Laceration Hazard
summary: The fuel canister that holds the wick of the torch has a sharp edge inside the lip of the opening that poses a laceration hazard when consumers try to remove the wick. Units: About 324,000 units.

title: Pacifiers Recalled by Antonio Flores Due to Choking Hazard
summary: The pacifier fails to meet federal safety standards. The nipple can separate from the base easily, the pacifier handle is too long, the mouth guard is too small and there are no ventilation holes on the mouth guard. The pacifier could pose a choking and aspiration hazard to young children. Units: Ab
